content: Trisodium phosphate (TSP), commonly found in white powder form at most hardware stores, is a chemical agent used for cleaning, stain removal, and degreasing. It is frequently employed to prepare surfaces for painting. Chemically, it is also referred to as trisodium orthophosphate and has the formula Na₃PO₄, though it is typically encountered in hydrated forms. TSP is a highly water-soluble ionic compound, and its aqueous solutions exhibit an alkaline pH. In addition to its cleaning applications, TSP is used as a food additive. In this context, it functions as an acidity regulator (buffering agent), emulsifier, thickening agent, nutrient fortifier, and sequestrant (metal-chelating agent). Collectively, sodium phosphates, including TSP, are often referred to as sodium phosphate or by the E number E339 when used in food products. TSP is also marketed as an over-the-counter enema in the United States, where it acts as a laxative to relieve constipation. However, it is important to distinguish TSP from related compounds such as sodium dihydrogen phosphate (monosodium phosphate or MSP) and disodium phosphate. Historically, similar phosphate-based chemicals were widely used in laundry and dishwashing detergents. However, due to their role as fertilizers that promote algal blooms in water bodies, the use of phosphate-containing products was restricted in the early 1970s. Today, products labeled as TSP Substitute, which typically contain 80–90% sodium carbonate, are marketed as alternatives. Cleaning products labeled as TSP may also contain other ingredients and may not be pure TSP; in some cases, they may consist of less than 50% TSP. Even regular TSP sold at hardware stores may be a mixture of TSP and TSP substitutes. Some large home improvement stores that sell paint no longer carry TSP. While TSP is an active ingredient in at least one type of toilet bowl cleaning tablet, it is generally not recommended for cleaning bathrooms because it can corrode metal surfaces. TSP is often used after cleaning with mineral spirits to remove any residual mineral spirits. It can also be combined with household chlorine bleach in the same solution, which is particularly effective for removing mildew from wood. However, TSP alone can cause dark stains on redwood, a problem that bleach can help prevent. TSP is also utilized in various industrial applications. It is used as a boiler treatment chemical to precipitate calcium and to regulate the caustic effects of disodium phosphate in coordinated phosphate chemistry. Additionally, TSP is employed to clean polyester filter elements in swimming pools.
